### Observed differences

- Routing out of A47 changed almost completely: in the earlier window about 96 in 100 of A47's outgoing transitions went to A28, while in the later window only about 1 in 100 does; A47 now spreads across A26 (about 22 in 100), A19, A27, A20 and A25 (about 15–16 in 100 each) plus minor targets, and A47 reaches A28 two to three steps later instead of immediately. [DIR011, LAG027]
- The five activities A19, A20, A25, A26 and A27 now lead almost exclusively to A28 (about 92–97 in 100 of their outgoing transitions each); earlier they split their exits between A34 and A30 (for example A19 about 53 to A34 and 41 to A30; A27 about 56 to A30 and 38 to A34). [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008]
- The order relative to A28 and A29 flipped: earlier A28 preceded A20, A25, A26 and A27 (for example A28 before A25 in about 24 in 100 traces, virtually never the reverse), whereas in the later window these activities precede A28 (about 18–25 in 100 traces); similarly, A29 preceded the group members earlier and now follows them. [REL016, REL018, REL020, REL023, REL015, REL017, REL019, REL021, REL024]
- The group members occur much earlier in the later window (mean positions about 0.31–0.34 of the trace versus about 0.6 earlier), while A47 remains in every trace with a nearly unchanged position (about 0.31 to 0.29). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]
- A29, A30 and A34 became a fixed, immediate tail: A29's transitions to A30 rose from about 51 to 95 in 100 and A30's to A34 from about 47 to 97 in 100; A29 is now followed by A30 after one step in about 96 in 100 cases (earlier about 52) and A30 by A34 after one step in about 97 in 100 (earlier about 47), whereas earlier A29 also fed A27, A25, A20, A19 and A26 (about 7–15 in 100 each), which no longer occurs. [DIR009, DIR010, REL022, LAG023, LAG024, LAG026]
- A08 receded sharply: it appears in about 23 in 100 later traces versus about 74 earlier, sits later when present (mean position about 0.24 to 0.45), and its outgoing transitions dispersed (to A16 from about 95 to 44 in 100, with A53 and A51 at about 12 each); A15 now routes to A16 in about 86 in 100 of its transitions (earlier about 60) and to A08 in about 6 (earlier about 40), and pairs with A08 now mostly occur without it (co-occurrence about 74 down to 23 in 100). [OCC003, POS001, DIR001, DIR003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL010, REL014]
- Several activities occur more often: A02 in about 21 versus 6 in 100 traces, A04 about 17 versus 4, A10 about 24 versus 8 and A17 about 33 versus 20; A14 and A15 now also lead to A02, A04, A06 and A10 in small shares (about 2–4 in 100 of their transitions). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC004, OCC005, DIR002, DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The 74 qualifying items (all control-flow) are many times the fewer than 1 expected if nothing had changed, so chance alone cannot account for the evidence as a whole. Within that, the evidence supports the possibility that the late-process block was rerouted and reordered: in the earlier window A47 led directly to A28, A28 preceded the group A19, A20, A25, A26, A27, whose exits split between A30 and A34 (with A30 often returning to the group) while A29 fed A30 and the group members; in the later window A47 leads into A19/A20/A25/A26/A27, each member proceeds almost always to A28, and A29, A30 and A34 form a fixed consecutive tail. The routing profiles of A47 and the group members were replaced almost wholesale, the pairwise orders flipped consistently in both relations (relative to A28 and to A29), the group's positions moved from about 60% to about a third of the trace, and step distances changed accordingly (A47 to A28 from one step to two–three; A29 to A30 and A30 to A34 now immediate) [DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, REL015, REL016, REL018, REL020, REL023, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, LAG023, LAG026, LAG027]. Limitations: the routing shares for the group members rest on roughly 30–52 traces per window, the many indicators describe one underlying rerouting rather than independent confirmations, and a shift in the mix of pre-existing variants cannot be distinguished from a rewritten flow on this evidence.

Other differences: A08 nearly disappeared (about 74 to 23 in 100 traces), occurs later when present, and lost its near-exclusive link to A16, with A15 now bypassing it directly to A16; in addition, A02, A04, A10 and A17 occur more often (for example A02 about 6 to 21 in 100 traces) and appear as new minor successors of A14 and A15. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, POS001, REL001, REL010]

Now let me understand the behavioural story.
